questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_4\) are the wavelengths of photons required to excite the Hydrogen atom from its ground state to its second and fourth excited states, respectively. What is the correct ratio \(\lambda_2 / \lambda_4\) ?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron of mass $m_e$ has a speed $u_n$ in the $n^{\text {th }}$ Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom. The normalized speed $V_n$ is given as $V_n=u_n / c=1 / 685$ and the mass of the electron in the units of energy is given as $M_e=m_e c^2=0.51 \times 10^6 \mathrm{eV}$, where $c$ is the velocity of light in vacuum. It is given that $\frac{\epsilon^2}{2 \varepsilon_0 h c}=1 / 137$. The Planck's constant $h$ is given as $4.13 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{eV}$-sec. The electron makes a transition from $n^{\text {th }}$ orbit to the ground state of the atom. What is the frequency of the emitted photon?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron in the ground state (with energy $E_1$ ) of a hydrogen atom, absorbs a photon of energy $E_a$, and gets excited to a higher energy level of principal quantum number $n$. What is the value of $n$ ?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider the Bohr model of an atom where an electron of charge $-e$ revolves around a nucleus of charge $+e$ in an orbit of radius $r$. The electron has an orbital angular momentum $2 \hbar$. If the nucleus had charge $+2 e$, what would have been the radius of the orbit of the electron with the same principal quantum number?
